{{Article header|deck=Sub-surface mining uses displacement missiles to extract deposits inside an asteroid.}}

'''Sub-surface mining''' uses a [[Sub-surface Displacement Missile]] against a deposit inside an asteroid. A prospector scan identifies the deposit, then the missile is fired and released during the extraction window to break material loose for collection.

{{Draft warning}}

== When to use sub-surface mining ==

Sub-surface mining sits between laser mining and core mining in complexity. The commander still prospects asteroids and collects refined cargo, but extraction depends on a short timing interaction rather than a continuous laser beam or a seismic detonation.

This method is useful when the target asteroid has sub-surface deposits worth extracting. It is not a replacement for prospecting: firing displacement missiles without a confirmed deposit wastes ammunition and time.

== Equipment ==

A sub-surface mining ship needs:

* [[Sub-surface Displacement Missile]] — extracts the internal deposit.
* [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] — identifies deposits and contents.
* [[Collector Limpet Controller]] — retrieves the released chunks.
* [[Refinery]], cargo space, and limpets.
* [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] — useful when the run is aimed at a mapped hotspot.

== Workflow summary ==

# Prospect the asteroid and select a sub-surface deposit.
# Fire and hold the displacement missile while tracking the deposit indicator.
# Release during the highlighted extraction band.
# Keep collector limpets active to retrieve the released chunks.
# Manage refinery bins so mixed fragments do not stall collection.

== Practical notes ==

* Sub-surface deposits are target-specific; do not expect every asteroid in a hotspot to contain one.
* Practice the release timing on low-risk targets before treating it as a profit run.
* Collectors and refinery bins are still the bottleneck once chunks have been released.
